citations.title: Classes of operating certificates
citations.requirement: Lists the OPWDD operating certificate classes for community residences: supervised community residence, supportive community residence, and individualized residential alternative (IRA).

citations.title: Part 686 Glossary (IRA, supervised IRA, supportive IRA, protective oversight)
citations.requirement: Defines IRA and the supervised and supportive IRA types. A supervised IRA has staff onsite or proximately available whenever residents are present.

citations.title: Certification of the facility class known as individualized residential alternative
citations.requirement: (a)(2)-(3): 9+ persons must meet 635-7.1, 7.2 and 7.3. 8 or fewer persons must meet the 635-7.1(h)(1)(ii) building code (NYC: 635-7.1(i)(1)(ii)) and 635-7.4(b)(3). If occupants cannot evacuate in 3 minutes or less, 635-7.2(a)(1)(iii) also applies. (a)(4): an IRA must meet 686.1-686.5, 686.9, 686.15(a)(1)-(3) and 686.16. (a)(5)-(6): protective oversight appropriate to need, with a site-specific written plan covering assessment of each person's supervision need (staff and/or technology), trained substitutes, supervisor qualifications and training, and periodic review. (a)(7): MHL 41.34 site selection applies to 4-14 bed IRAs with onsite supervision and 1-3 bed IRAs with 24-hour supervision. (b): OPWDD verifies the facility evacuation plan, staff and resident training and evaluation, a current fire-evacuation evaluation in each ISP (8 or fewer beds), an annual review of each person's protective oversight plan, supervisor first-aid training, and fire alarms audible in sleeping areas with doors closed (8 or fewer beds).

citations.title: Utilization of temporary use beds and vacant beds
citations.requirement: IRAs of four or more beds may designate temporary use beds on the operating certificate. Temporary use beds count toward certified capacity. 686.15(a)(1)-(3) applies to IRAs through 686.16(a)(4).

citations.title: Staffing (community residences)
citations.requirement: (a)(1)-(2): personnel must be available to supervise, operate and maintain the premises, and there must be a staffing plan based on the number of individuals, their level of functioning and need, support staff needs and physical plant demands. (a)(3): volunteers may not substitute for paid personnel. Family and friends are not counted as volunteers. (a)(4): in a supervised residence, staff must be available whenever individuals are present. Less intensive coverage is allowed only on a documented individual assessment in the plan of services. (b)(1): a written staffing schedule at the site shows supervision available or on call 24 hours a day. (b)(2): a written volunteer utilization plan if volunteers are used. The rule sets no numeric ratio.

citations.title: Governance (community residences)
citations.requirement: Applies to IRAs via 686.16(a)(4). Section number and title are confirmed in the Part 686 table of contents. Section text was not fetched, so pull it before drafting governing-body content.

citations.title: Administration (community residences)
citations.requirement: Section number and title are confirmed in the Part 686 table of contents. Section text was not fetched. 686.6 is not listed in 686.16(a)(4), so confirm its applicability to IRAs before citing it as an IRA requirement.

citations.title: Fee-setting and financial reporting for voluntary-operated community residences
citations.requirement: Section number and title are confirmed in the Part 686 table of contents. Section text was not fetched. Applicability to IRAs is not confirmed because 686.13 is not listed in 686.16(a)(4).

citations.title: Recordkeeping (community residences)
citations.requirement: Section number and title are confirmed in the Part 686 table of contents. Section text was not fetched. It is not listed in 686.16(a)(4), so confirm applicability to IRAs.

citations.title: Physical plant, Life Safety Code and environmental requirements referenced by 686.16; Uniform Code enforcement for IRAs via 635-7.4(a)(3)
citations.requirement: Building, Life Safety Code and environmental standards that 686.16 incorporates for IRAs. NYS DOS guidance identifies 635-7.4(a)(3) as the Uniform Code enforcement route for OPWDD IRAs.

citations.title: Safety and welfare requirements for all facilities (except family care homes and IRAs housing eight or fewer persons)
citations.requirement: Applies to supervised community residences and IRAs housing nine or more persons. One listed requirement is documentation that all heat and smoke-detecting alarm devices are tested quarterly (635-7.3(e)(i)(1)).

citations.title: Rights and responsibilities of persons receiving services
citations.requirement: (a)(3): rights limitations must be documented, individual, time-limited and for clinical purposes only. (a)(4): enumerated rights (safe and sanitary environment; freedom from abuse, corporal punishment, unnecessary mechanical restraint and unnecessary medication; confidentiality; written individualized plan with right to participate, object and appeal; choice of physician and dentist; sexuality and family planning information; religion; voting; use of personal money; balanced diet; own clothing; privacy; storage; request an alternative residence; grievances without reprisal; visitors and communication; health care proxy; gender expression). (a)(4)(xv): information before admission on supplies and services provided and charges. (a)(6): staff are advised of rights. (a)(7): rights are not limited for staff convenience, as a threat, as retribution or for discipline. (a)(8): rights and conduct rules are given at or before admission and after changes, in the primary language. (a)(9): objections under 633.12. (a)(10): written requests for clinical record access under MHL 33.16, with denial review by the OPWDD Clinical Record Access Review Committee. (a)(11): health care proxy duties. (a)(12): advise of complaint contacts on admission and as they change. (a)(15): language access with no charge for interpreters.

citations.title: Training of employees, volunteers, family care providers and persons receiving services with regard to their safety and the prevention of abuse
citations.requirement: (b)(1): training within 3 months of hire or start of volunteering on human growth and development, characteristics of persons served, promoting positive relationships, abuse prevention/identification/reporting/processing, laws and policies on protection from abuse, incident reporting, and safety and security procedures including fire safety. (b)(2): annual retraining on positive relationships, abuse prevention and reporting, laws and policies, incident reporting, and safety/security including fire safety. (a)(1)(viii)-(ix): training on preventing and managing significant-risk body substance exposure (HIV). (b)(3): a mechanism to monitor type, frequency and amount of training, with current records and employee concurrence on interview. (a)(2), (b)(4): self-protection training for individuals identified by the program planning team. (b)(5): one-time board training applies only to not-for-profit corporations.

citations.title: Management of personal funds
citations.requirement: Applies to all OPWDD-certified residential facilities. Policies must reflect the agency's fiduciary duty under MHL 33.07(e) when it manages funds. Policies must address at minimum security, staff accountability, paper and electronic recordkeeping, usage, and monitoring of personal allowance and other income. Personal allowance is the monthly income portion for the individual's personal expenditure. Management is the SSL 131-o offer to set up separate accounting. Records of compliance are kept 4 years per OPWDD's regulations page. Only excerpts of the section were retrieved.

citations.title: Protection of individuals receiving services in facilities operated and/or certified by OPWDD (behavior support)
citations.requirement: Applies to all OPWDD-certified residential facilities. Definitions reviewed: behavior plan/human rights committee; informed consent committee; functional behavior assessment; behavior support plan as a component of the plan of services; restrictive/intrusive interventions (intermediate and restrictive physical intervention, exclusionary time-out, mechanical restraining devices, behavior medication without a co-occurring psychiatric diagnosis, and other agency-designated methods); physical intervention categories (protective, intermediate, restrictive); modified clothing as a mechanical restraint; rights limitations; aversive conditioning; Level 1 and Level 2 Behavioral Intervention Specialist qualifications; program planning team composition. Operative subdivisions (d)-(j) were not retrieved.

citations.title: Medication (including vitamins)
citations.requirement: Required of all residential facilities. Each agency develops its own medication policies. Staff may administer only if they hold a job description with direct care duties and have completed an OPWDD-approved course and practicum and been certified or recertified within the year (a)(14)(iii)(c). Medical or nursing supervision of medication staff is required (a)(15). A program planning team evaluates self-administration ability with RN, physician or PA input, no later than 3 months after admission, and reviews it at least annually (a)(16). A separate administration record per person (name, medication/dose/route, date/time, signature) is required (a)(17). Annual medication regimen review by an RN, physician, PA or pharmacist (a)(18). Locked storage; double-locked controlled substances (non-supportive residences); separate locked container for medications in a food refrigerator (a)(19). OTC medication needs written practitioner approval at least annually and is limited to 2 days without practitioner direction (a)(13). Medication is suspended and the practitioner told immediately on a significant adverse reaction (a)(14)(ii). Disposal rules in (a)(20) were only partly retrieved.

citations.title: Criminal history record checks
citations.requirement: Applies to OPWDD-certified facilities and HCBS waiver services. (c)(1): designate authorized parties and submit their name, position and contact information to the Justice Center. (c)(2): written policies covering which applicants are subject to checks, safety and oversight of temporarily approved provisional staff and volunteers, notification to the Justice Center when a party ceases to be a subject party, and handling of later convictions or pending charges. (d)(2): checks are required for prospective employees and operators (natural persons with an ownership interest) with regular and substantial unsupervised contact. This is presumed for direct care in residential facilities (ICFs, CRs, IRAs), residential habilitation staff, supervisors of direct care staff, drivers and escorts, clinicians, care managers, and anyone assigned to a certified site. Also required on a change in ownership. (e): process under Part 701 (701.5). (f): provisional approval is allowed only without unsupervised physical contact, with monitoring by a trained employee and an attestation. Only the first part of the section was retrieved.

citations.requirement: Section number and title are confirmed in the Part 633 table of contents. 633.4(a)(11) and (a)(4)(xxvi) describe facility duties. Section text was not fetched.

citations.requirement: Section number and title are confirmed in the Part 633 table of contents. 633.22(d)(3) cross-references it. Text was not fetched.

citations.requirement: Section number and title are confirmed in the Part 633 table of contents. A Sept 2026 OPWDD memo says OPWDD is adding or amending 633.9 and conforming 633.15, so the Part 633 text may be changing. Check the current text before finalizing.

citations.requirement: Section number and title are confirmed in the Part 633 table of contents. Text was not fetched.

citations.title: Medical treatment
citations.requirement: Section number and title are confirmed in the Part 633 table of contents. Text was not fetched.

citations.title: [Expired] Training Flexibilities
citations.requirement: The Cornell LII Part 633 table of contents lists this section as [Expired]. The earlier research described commissioner flexibilities during extreme staffing shortages. Do not build any policy on it. Staff must complete the full 633.8 and 633.17 training.

citations.title: Notable occurrences, defined
citations.requirement: On and after 1/1/2016: serious notable occurrences are (a) the death of any person receiving services regardless of cause, including all deaths of residents of OPWDD-certified residences, and (b) sensitive situations, which agency policy must define and which include possible criminal acts by an individual. Minor notable occurrences are suspected theft or financial exploitation over $15 and up to $100 (isolated, no card involved) and injury needing treatment beyond first aid by a physician, dentist, PA or NP. A death that is also a reportable incident is reported both ways. The pre-2016 text, retained in the section, covered unauthorized absence, choking and larger thefts, which are now reportable incidents under 624.3.

citations.title: Reporting, recording, and investigation
citations.requirement: (a)(1): written policies on reporting, recording, investigation, review and monitoring; the reporting duties of employees, interns, volunteers, consultants and contractors; and notice to employees that every reportable incident is investigated and that an investigation continues to a substantiated or unsubstantiated finding even if the employee leaves. All employees, interns, volunteers, consultants and contractors must report. Minor notable occurrences go to the CEO or designee within 48 hours. Reportable incidents and serious notable occurrences go to the CEO or designee immediately, and to OPWDD immediately. IRMA updates are due at least monthly until closure. Only the first part of the section was retrieved from search text.

citations.title: Reportable incidents, defined
citations.requirement: Cross-referenced in 624.4 and 624.5. The section text was not fetched, so the current categories (abuse/neglect and significant incidents such as missing person, choking with known risk and inappropriate use of restraints) must be pulled from the regulation before drafting definitions.

citations.title: The Part 624 and Part 625 Handbook
citations.requirement: OPWDD guidance. Reportable incidents in OPWDD-certified programs go to the Justice Center VPCR at 1-855-373-2122 and to OPWDD under 624.5. Deliberate inappropriate use of restraints is abuse/neglect. Inappropriate use of restraints is a significant incident.

citations.cite: NYS Justice Center - Mandated Reporters (VPCR hotline)
citations.title: Mandated Reporters
citations.requirement: Employees and volunteers of certified or operated facilities are mandated reporters. They report when they have reasonable cause to suspect a reportable incident, via the 24-hour VPCR hotline at 1-855-373-2122 (Relay: dial 711 and give the number).

citations.cite: NYS Justice Center Criminal Background Check (CBC) program; MHL 16.33
citations.title: Criminal Background Check (CBC)
citations.requirement: Providers designate Authorized Persons to register applicants for fingerprinting (IdentoGO) and receive results.

citations.title: Criminal history checks for prospective OPWDD employees and volunteers
citations.requirement: OPWDD providers request checks for prospective employees and volunteers, submitted through OPWDD per the Justice Center CBC page. The statute text was not fetched; the cite and its application are taken from the research and the Justice Center page.

citations.title: Person-centered planning; Documentation of rights modifications
citations.requirement: From OPWDD's final regulation text, effective 11/1/2015. Applies to OPWDD-funded HCBS waiver services. The plan must document, for a certified residential setting, that the residence was chosen by the individual and which alternatives were considered. The plan is updated when it is ineffective and on reassessment of functional need. 636-1.4: modifications to the specified HCBS rights need a specific assessed need and justification in the person-centered service plan. 633.4 and 633.16 hold the related documentation rules.

citations.title: HCBS general requirements (integrated settings)
citations.requirement: From an OPWDD regulatory filing excerpt. HCBS must be delivered in integrated settings that do not isolate individuals. Setting qualities include a physically accessible setting. Any modification must be supported by a specific assessed need, justified and documented. Confirm against the current codified text, as this was a filing excerpt.

citations.title: Admission to and services in certified residential opportunities
citations.requirement: Subpart 636-3 (effective 3/14/2023) governs admission. OPWDD assigns Emergency Need, Substantial Need or Current Need. Certified residences must promptly report vacancies so each is first considered for people with Emergency Need.

citations.title: Responsibilities of care management providers
citations.requirement: Care managers confirm OPWDD eligibility and a residential request before referral.

citations.title: Residential habilitation in a community residence under the OPWDD HCBS waiver
citations.requirement: Defines residential habilitation in a community residence under the OPWDD 1915(c) HCBS waiver. Providers must be approved by OPWDD and DOH and be Medicaid-enrolled to be paid.

citations.title: Rates for residential habilitation services
citations.requirement: One provider-wide residential habilitation rate per provider.

citations.title: Supervised IRA residential habilitation: daily unit, rate codes, retainer days
citations.requirement: Daily unit of service. Rate codes cover service day, therapeutic/non-medical leave day and retainer/medical leave day. At most 14 retainer days per person per rate year. Research flags that it is not confirmed still in effect.

citations.title: IRA Residential Habilitation Service Documentation
citations.requirement: Dated guidance on IRA residential habilitation documentation. Research flags the supportive IRA 11-day minimum as status-unverified. Confirm it is current before use.

citations.cite: OMIG Audit Protocol - OPWDD IRA Residential Habilitation
citations.title: OMIG audit protocol
citations.requirement: OMIG audits IRA residential habilitation claims for documentation and rate-code compliance. A claim is disallowed if the documentation does not match the rate code billed.

citations.title: Personal allowance and room and board cost responsibilities
citations.requirement: Sets resident room and board and cost-of-care responsibilities and the personal allowance. For community residences including IRAs, the maximum monthly cost of care is the Level II SSI combined payment level minus the SSL 131-o minimum personal allowance. Supervised IRAs are responsible for required supplies and services under 635.9.

citations.cite: OPWDD Personal Allowance Manual (2023) and Protecting Personal Allowance advisory (Oct 2023)
citations.title: Personal allowance guidance
citations.requirement: Providers must have written procedures to handle, store and audit personal allowance. Staff are trained on them. Each person's funds are tracked separately. Funds are locked with limited access and staff accountability. There is a ledger of all receipts, disbursements and cash balance. Cash equivalents such as prepaid cards are treated as cash. Cash above the cash cap needs documentation of a specific purpose and is limited to 14 days. Annual personal expenditure planning is required when the agency manages the allowance.

citations.title: Fire safety: evacuation and fire drill frequency
citations.requirement: Standardizes minimum frequencies of evacuation and fire drills in homes and day settings. Evacuation and fire drills are generally procedurally synonymous. Drills may be varied for a few specific reasons, but the minimum number of full evacuation drills must still be met. Homes certified under the Health Care chapters of the Life Safety Code cannot use defend-in-place for non-fire evacuations. The numeric minimums were not captured, so pull the ADM text.

citations.cite: OPWDD Health and Safety Alert (July 2018) - HCBS Settings 'access to food'; 42 CFR 441.301(c)(4)(vi); 14 NYCRR 636-1.4
citations.title: Access to food in HCBS settings
citations.requirement: Individuals are entitled to access to food at any time. Restrictions run from least restrictive (all foods, all the time) to most restrictive through the person-centered planning process, and must be justified under 636-1.4.

citations.title: IRA Operating Certificate Application
citations.requirement: IRA operating certificate application. Listed processing time is 90 to 120 days. The term is triennial, with a maximum of 3 years. Denials are based on the inspection outcome.

citations.cite: eMedNY OPWDD Waiver Provider Enrollment; Community Residence enrollment (category of service 0269)
citations.title: Provider enrollment
citations.requirement: Enrollment requires an IRS SS-4 letter (a W-9 is not accepted) and certification of a Provider Compliance Program. Community residence enrollment is filed under category of service 0269.

citations.title: IRA Facilities
citations.requirement: A 1994 NYC DOB notice tied the final Certificate of Occupancy for IRAs to the IRA license. Current status is unverified, so ask DOB.

citations.title: Site selection (as applied to IRAs by 14 NYCRR 686.16(a)(7))
citations.requirement: Applies to IRAs of 4-14 beds with onsite supervision and 1-3 beds with 24-hour supervision, per 686.16(a)(7). The statute text was not fetched.

citations.cite: OPWDD memo to provider associations (Sept 2026) - new 14 NYCRR 633.9 / conforming changes to 633.15
citations.title: Representative payee rulemaking
citations.requirement: OPWDD is amending Part 633 to add or amend 633.9 on representative payees for residents of certified residences, with conforming changes to 633.15 on managing personal allowance. Confirm the adopted text before finalizing the funds policy.

citations.title: Mandated reporter definition and duty to report to the Justice Center
citations.requirement: Secondary source (Albany Law Government Law Center explainer endnotes) points to SSL 491 for mandated reporting and SSL 488(5), (5-a) for the definition. Statute text was not fetched.

citations.cite: Jonathan's Law (per NYS Justice Center Investigations Guidance, 2025)
citations.title: Notification and access to incident information
citations.requirement: Jonathan's Law requires notification and access to information about incidents at OPWDD-certified, operated or licensed providers. The statute section number is not stated in the retrieved text. Pull the statute and 624.5 for notice timeframes.

citations.cite: OPWDD Request for Approval to Fill a Residential Opportunity
citations.title: DDRO Director approval of placements
citations.requirement: Every placement into a certified residence requires approval of the DDRO Director before admission, using OPWDD's request form.

citations.cite: NYS Justice Center - What to Expect if You Are Involved in a Justice Center Investigation (Oct 2021)
citations.title: Mandated reporter timing; Category 2 findings
citations.requirement: A mandated reporter with reasonable cause to suspect a reportable incident reports immediately to the VPCR. Reporting may be delayed for safety or to call 911, but the report must be made within 24 hours of discovery. A final Category 2 finding is reported to OPWDD providers in the Staff Exclusion List check. It is not an automatic bar to employment but is a factor in the hiring decision.

policies.title: Referral, Need Determination and Admission Decision
state_specifics: Care managers must confirm OPWDD eligibility and a residential request before referral (14 NYCRR 636-3.5). Ask for this documentation with every referral.
The DDRO Director must approve every placement before admission, using the Request for Approval to Fill a Residential Opportunity.
OPWDD assigns Emergency Need, Substantial Need or Current Need. Report each vacancy promptly so Emergency Need is considered first (24-ADM-03).
The need determination covers the applicant's need for service, the ability to meet ongoing needs, and family intactness and geographic proximity.
Staff and the applicant take part in the determination, including the final admission decision. Written admission procedures are required.

policies.title: Admission Criteria and Pre-Admission Review
state_specifics: Admission criteria must be written in functional terms.
Before admission, review a medical/physical examination dated within 90 days before the review.
Before admission, also review assessment(s) of strengths, needs, interests and living skills completed within 90 days before the review.
Document the review in the admission file before requesting DDRO approval.

policies.title: Voluntary Admission, Nondiscrimination and Written Disclosure of Charges
federal: Title VI of the Civil Rights Act
state_specifics: No person is admitted over his or her objection except by court order.

No person is excluded for race, religion, color, age, gender, national origin or inability to pay. Written admission criteria may limit age range, level of disability or gender only when necessitated by the facility's overall objective.

Before admission, and again as changes occur, give the applicant (or parent, guardian or correspondent) written notice of charges and of the supplies and services provided, unless a capable adult objects to notice to others.
The charge notice must be consistent with 635.9 (maximum cost of care tied to SSI Level II minus the SSL 131-o personal allowance) and 633.4(a)(4)(xv).
Give the rights and conduct rules at or before admission, in the person's primary language.

policies.title: Discharge Criteria and Avoiding Precipitous Discharge
state_specifics: Written discharge criteria are required.

Make and document reasonable efforts to meet the person's needs before a more restrictive placement is sought or discharge is contemplated. Weigh the needs of other residents and the facility's available resources.
Individuals may request an alternative residence (633.4(a)(4)).
Report vacancies created by discharge to OPWDD promptly (24-ADM-03).

policies.title: Discharge Procedures, Freedom to Leave and Discharge Planning
state_specifics: Written procedures are required for being discharged, including discharge against the recommendation of the program planning team.
No overt or covert physical or psychological pressure may be used to stop a person who wants to leave.
Those responsible for program planning take part in designing the discharge plan and coordinating services.
The person may object to a discharge or placement decision through the 633.12 objection process (pull the text for timelines).

policies.title: Review and Appeal of Plans of Services and Placement Decisions
state_specifics: Individuals, parents, guardians and correspondents may appeal the plan of services and placement decisions.
Individuals have the right to participate in their plan, object and appeal (633.4(a)(4)).
Objections go through the 633.12 process. Insert the timelines from the regulation text.
Give appeal information at or before admission and after any change, in the primary language (633.4(a)(8)).
Appeal procedures must conform to the Commissioner's regulations.

policies.title: Grievances and Complaints
state_specifics: Individuals may file grievances without reprisal (633.4(a)(4)).
Tell individuals the complaint contacts on admission and whenever they change (633.4(a)(12)).
Allegations of abuse or neglect are not grievances. Send them to the VPCR hotline 1-855-373-2122 (24 hours; Relay: dial 711 and give the number).
Provide interpreters at no charge (633.4(a)(15)).

policies.title: Community Involvement, Integration and Employment Choice
state_specifics: Give staff and individuals direction on activities that promote and nurture the residence's involvement with its neighborhood and community.
The person-centered plan documents that the individual chose the residence and which alternatives were considered (636-1).
Services are delivered in integrated settings that do not isolate individuals (636-2; confirm against codified text).
Any limit on community access is a rights modification that needs a documented assessed need (636-1.4).

policies.title: Individual Participation in Day-to-Day Decisions
state_specifics: Define how individuals, within their capability, contribute to day-to-day decisions (menus, schedules, house activities, décor).
Individuals have access to food at any time. Any restriction is justified under 636-1.4 through person-centered planning.
Record individual and staff involvement in neighborhood and community activities.
Rights are never limited for staff convenience, as a threat, as retribution or for discipline (633.4(a)(7)).

policies.title: Informed Consent, Health Care Proxy and Decision-Making Support
state_specifics: Individuals have the right to choose their physician and dentist and to use a health care proxy (633.4(a)(4), (a)(11)).
Follow the 633.20 health care proxy and 633.18 DNR procedures. Pull the section text before finalizing.
Behavior interventions with restrictions need informed consent and review under 633.16 (Informed Consent Committee).
Capable adults decide for themselves. Involve guardians or correspondents as the person's status requires.

policies.category: Administration of records, incidents/abuse and medication (686.6(a)(2)(vi))
policies.title: Plans of Services: Development, Implementation and Daily Documentation
state_specifics: Each person has a written individualized plan with the right to participate, object and appeal (633.4).
The plan is updated when ineffective and on reassessment of functional need (636-1).
Include each person's protective oversight plan and a current fire-evacuation evaluation in the plan (686.16(b)).
Daily service notes must support the rate code billed. OMIG disallows claims where documentation does not match the code.

policies.category: Administration of records, incidents/abuse and medication (686.6(a)(2)(vi))
policies.title: Personal Funds and Financial Records
state_specifics: Written procedures must address security, staff accountability, paper and electronic recordkeeping, usage and monitoring of personal allowance (633.15). Records are kept 4 years.
Track each person's funds separately. Keep them locked with limited access. Keep a ledger of all receipts, disbursements and cash balance. Treat prepaid cards as cash.
Cash above the cap needs a documented specific purpose and is limited to 14 days.
Maximum monthly cost of care is the Level II SSI combined payment level minus the SSL 131-o minimum personal allowance (635.9).
OPWDD is amending 633.9 and 633.15 (representative payee rules). Check the adopted text before finalizing.

policies.category: Administration of records, incidents/abuse and medication (686.6(a)(2)(vi))
policies.title: Confidentiality and Protection of Individuals' Records (Privacy and HIPAA)
state_specifics: Individuals have the right to confidentiality (633.4(a)(4)).
Written requests for clinical record access follow MHL 33.16. A denial can be reviewed by the OPWDD Clinical Record Access Review Committee (633.4(a)(10)).
HIV-related information is confidential under 633.19, PHL Article 27-F and 10 NYCRR Part 63.
Jonathan's Law governs notice and access to incident information for families.

policies.category: Administration of records, incidents/abuse and medication (686.6(a)(2)(vi))
policies.title: Statistical Information and Required Reports to the State
state_specifics: Name who coordinates, collects, releases and tracks statistical information.
Enter reportable incidents and serious notable occurrences in OPWDD's incident system and update at least monthly until closure (624.5).
Keep a log of minor notable occurrences.
Confirm the 686.14 recordkeeping requirements apply before relying on them.

policies.category: Administration of records, incidents/abuse and medication (686.6(a)(2)(vi))
policies.title: Incidents, Allegations of Abuse, Notable Occurrences and Investigations
state_specifics: Report reasonable cause to suspect a reportable incident immediately to the Justice Center VPCR hotline at 1-855-373-2122 (24 hours; Relay: dial 711 and give the number).
Reporting may be delayed for safety or to call 911, but the VPCR report must be made within 24 hours of discovery.

Serious notable occurrences (every death, and sensitive situations as defined by agency policy) and reportable incidents go to the CEO or designee and to OPWDD immediately. Minor notable occurrences go to the CEO or designee within 48 hours (624.5).
An investigation continues to a substantiated or unsubstantiated finding even if the employee leaves. All employees, interns, volunteers, consultants and contractors must report.
Follow Jonathan's Law notice to families. Pull the notice timeframes from 624.5.

policies.category: Administration of records, incidents/abuse and medication (686.6(a)(2)(vi))
policies.title: Abuse, Neglect and Exploitation Prevention and Mandated Reporting
state_specifics: Employees and volunteers are mandated reporters.
Train within 3 months of hire and annually on abuse prevention, identification and reporting and on laws and policies (633.8(b)).
Deliberate inappropriate use of restraints is abuse/neglect. Inappropriate use of restraints is a significant incident.
Individuals have the right to freedom from abuse, corporal punishment, and unnecessary restraint or medication (633.4(a)(4)).
Self-protection training goes to individuals identified by the program planning team (633.8).

policies.category: Administration of records, incidents/abuse and medication (686.6(a)(2)(vi))
policies.title: Medication Administration, Staff Certification and Self-Administration Training
state_specifics: Only staff with direct care duties who have completed the OPWDD-approved course and practicum and are certified or recertified within the year may administer (633.17(a)(14)). Track current certification status.
Medical or nursing supervision is required. The program planning team evaluates self-administration within 3 months of admission, with RN, physician or PA input, and reviews it at least annually.
Keep a separate administration record per person (medication, dose, route, date/time, staff signature). An RN, physician, PA or pharmacist reviews the regimen annually.
Lock storage. Double-lock controlled substances (non-supportive). Use a separate locked container in a food refrigerator.

OTC medication needs practitioner approval at least annually and is limited to 2 days without practitioner direction. Suspend medication on a significant adverse reaction and notify the practitioner immediately.

policies.category: Administration of records, incidents/abuse and medication (686.6(a)(2)(vi))
policies.title: Individual Records, Retention and Access
state_specifics: Specify the contents of each individual's record: admission review, plan, notes, health, rights modifications and funds ledger.
Retention periods: personal funds records 4 years. Confirm the OPWDD and OMIG retention period for other records. It was not verified.
Individuals may request access in writing (633.4(a)(10)).
Confirm that 686.14 applies before citing it.

policies.title: Medical Emergencies and Change of Condition
state_specifics: Define the staff actions for a medical emergency and how staff are familiarized with them.
Notify the practitioner immediately of a significant adverse medication reaction (633.17).
Treatment beyond first aid by a physician, dentist, PA or NP is at least a minor notable occurrence (624.4).
Health care proxy and DNR orders are handled under 633.20 and 633.18.

policies.title: Emergency Preparedness, Disasters, Fire Drills and Evacuation
state_specifics: Evacuation procedures must meet the special needs of persons with developmental disabilities. Record each person's evacuation ability.
Occupants who cannot evacuate in 3 minutes or less trigger 635-7.2(a)(1)(iii).
For 9+ beds, test heat and smoke alarms quarterly (635-7.3(e)(i)(1)). For 8 or fewer beds, fire alarms must be audible in sleeping areas with doors closed (686.16(b)).
Evacuation and fire drill minimum frequencies come from OPWDD ADM #2012-02. Insert the numbers from the ADM text.
Homes certified under the Health Care chapters of the Life Safety Code cannot use defend-in-place for non-fire evacuations.

policies.title: Death of an Individual
state_specifics: Every death of a resident of an OPWDD-certified residence is a serious notable occurrence, regardless of cause (624.4).
If the death is also a reportable incident, report it both ways.
Notify the CEO or designee and OPWDD immediately (624.5).
Notify the family or correspondent under Jonathan's Law and the individual's wishes or health care proxy. Pull the notice timeframes.

policies.title: Health and Safety Program
state_specifics: Individuals have the right to a safe and sanitary environment (633.4(a)(4)).
Define a smoking policy under 633.23 (pull the text).
Cover hazard reporting, hazardous materials, safe storage and staff health and safety training.
Review the plan after incidents and during quality improvement.

policies.title: Nursing Oversight and Health Care Coordination
state_specifics: Medical or nursing supervision of medication-administering staff is required (633.17(a)(15)).
An RN, physician, PA or pharmacist performs the annual medication regimen review.
Required nursing hours were not verified. Set the nursing plan from individual needs and confirm with the regional office.
Coordinate routine and specialty care and follow up on practitioner orders.

policies.title: Health Monitoring, Seizures and Choking Risk
state_specifics: Choking with a known risk is a significant incident under current 624.3 categories. Pull the 624.3 text before finalizing.
Write individual seizure and choking protocols into the plan.
Treatment beyond first aid by a physician, dentist, PA or NP is a minor notable occurrence (624.4).
Supervisors with oversight responsibility need first-aid training (686.16(b)).

policies.title: Infection Prevention and Control
state_specifics: Train staff on preventing and managing significant-risk body substance exposure (633.8(a)(1)(viii)-(ix)).
HIV information is confidential (633.19, PHL Article 27-F).
Employee TB control follows 633.14. Pull the text for screening schedules.
Follow the OSHA bloodborne pathogens standard.

policies.title: Food, Nutrition and Modified Diets
state_specifics: Individuals have a right to a balanced diet (633.4(a)(4)).
Individuals have access to food at any time. Any restriction is justified under 636-1.4 and documented in the plan.
Supervised IRAs provide the required supplies and services under 635.9.
Document modified diets, choking risk and practitioner orders in the plan.

policies.title: Transportation and Vehicle Safety
state_specifics: Drivers and escorts are presumed to have regular and substantial unsupervised contact and need criminal history checks (633.22(d)(2)).
Confirm insurance and driver requirements with OPWDD. No specific standard was found.
Include safety procedures in staff training (633.8).
Accessible transport must meet each person's mobility needs.

policies.title: Residential Environment and Accessibility
state_specifics: Eight or fewer residents follow the 635-7.1(h)(1)(ii) building code (NYC: 635-7.1(i)(1)(ii)) and 635-7.4(b)(3). Nine or more follow 635-7.1, 7.2 and 7.3.
Uniform Code enforcement for OPWDD IRAs runs through 635-7.4(a)(3).
Site selection under MHL 41.34 applies to 4-14 bed IRAs with onsite supervision.
In NYC, confirm the status of the 1994 DOB notice (TPPN #9/94) on the Certificate of Occupancy.
HCBS settings must be physically accessible (636-2; confirm against codified text).

policies.title: Recruitment, Hiring, Residence Manager Qualifications and Job Performance Evaluation
federal: Title VII of the Civil Rights Act
state_specifics: Residence manager: written criteria require at least a high school diploma or equivalent and at least 1 year of experience working with persons with developmental disabilities.
Policy covers the hiring process, qualifications, education and skills required, job descriptions, duties and responsibilities, and performance evaluations.
Review applicant backgrounds under 633.5 and 633.24 (pull the texts).
Supervisory requirements follow 633.6.

policies.title: Direct Support Professional Orientation, Training and In-Service
state_specifics: Within 3 months of hire or start of volunteering, train on human growth and development, characteristics of persons served, positive relationships, abuse prevention and reporting, incident reporting, and safety and security including fire safety (633.8(b)(1)).
Retrain annually on the same core topics (633.8(b)(2)).
Keep a training-monitoring mechanism with current records (633.8(b)(3)). Coordinate development with individual and staff needs and use community training resources.
Medication staff complete the OPWDD-approved course and practicum (633.17).
The 633.27 training flexibility is listed as expired. Plan on full training.

policies.title: Staff Concerns Without Threat of Job Loss and Nondiscrimination in Employment
federal: Title VII of the Civil Rights Act
state_specifics: Provide a means for staff to raise matters of concern without threat of job loss.
Prohibit discrimination in hiring and promotion based on race, religion, color, gender, national origin, age or disability.
Staff may report abuse or neglect directly to the VPCR hotline at 1-855-373-2122.
Staff are notified that every reportable incident is investigated (624.5).

policies.title: Criminal History Checks, Background Checks and Employee Registries
state_specifics: Designate Authorized Parties and submit their name, position and contact information to the Justice Center (633.22(c)(1)).

Checks are required for prospective employees and operators with regular and substantial unsupervised contact (633.22(d)(2)). This includes direct care staff, supervisors, drivers, escorts and clinicians. Also check on change of ownership.
Provisional staff may work only without unsupervised physical contact, with monitoring by a trained employee and an attestation (633.22(f)).
Fingerprinting is through IdentoGO. Requests go through OPWDD (MHL 16.34).
A final Category 2 finding is not an automatic bar but must be weighed. Document the decision.

policies.title: Employee Health and TB Screening
state_specifics: Follow 14 NYCRR 633.14 TB control procedures. Pull the text for who is screened and the schedule.
Keep health records in a confidential file separate from the personnel file.
Cover exposure follow-up under the HIV and body-substance training (633.8(a)(1)(viii)-(ix)).

policies.title: Personnel Records
state_specifics: Each file holds the job description, qualifications, evaluations, criminal history check outcome, medication certification and training records.
Training records must be current and available (633.8(b)(3)).
Keep medication certification dates current (633.17).
Confirm the retention period with OPWDD. It was not verified.

policies.title: Staff Conduct and Professional Boundaries
state_specifics: Follow 633.7 on conduct of employees, volunteers, family care providers and custodians (pull the text).
Rights may not be limited for staff convenience or as discipline (633.4(a)(7)).
Cover theft and financial exploitation reporting (624.4 thresholds) and personal funds handling (633.15).
Include boundaries with individuals' funds, property and relationships.

policies.title: Staffing Plan, Schedule and Supervision Coverage
state_specifics: Keep a written staffing plan based on number of individuals, level of functioning and need, support staff needs and physical plant demands (686.9(a)).
In a supervised residence, staff must be available whenever individuals are present. Less intensive coverage is allowed only on a documented individual assessment in the plan of services.
Keep a written staffing schedule at the site showing supervision available or on call 24 hours a day.
686.9 sets no numeric ratio and no awake-overnight rule. Volunteers may not substitute for paid personnel.

policies.category: Policy approval process and governing body role (686.6(a)(2)(x))
policies.title: Organization, Governing Body and Program Director Responsibilities
state_specifics: Define the governing body's role in approving policies.
Pull the 686.5 governance text before drafting. It applies to IRAs through 686.16(a)(4).
Name the person responsible for the residence (residence manager) and the executive.

policies.category: Policy approval process and governing body role (686.6(a)(2)(x))
policies.title: Policy Review, Approval and Document Control
state_specifics: Describe the approval process and the governing body's role.
Policies cover admission, discharge, appeals, community involvement, decision-making, records, incidents and abuse, medication, emergencies, health and safety, and personnel (686.6(a)(2)).
Review annually and after regulatory changes. Part 633 may change: OPWDD is amending 633.9 and 633.15.
Keep version dates and approval signatures.

policies.category: Policy approval process and governing body role (686.6(a)(2)(x))
policies.title: Policy and Procedure Manual: Contents and Public Availability
state_specifics: The manual is a public document. Make it available to individuals, parents, guardians, correspondents, staff and others.

The manual must contain: admission and discharge; administration of records; emergencies and disasters; health and safety; personnel; review and appeal procedures; community involvement; and individuals' involvement in residence activities.
Keep a copy at the site.
Provide rights and conduct rules in the person's primary language (633.4(a)(8)).

policies.category: IRA site-specific protective oversight plan and evacuation plan (686.16)
policies.title: Site-Specific Protective Oversight Plan
state_specifics: Provide protective oversight appropriate to each person's needs (686.16(a)(5)).

Write a site-specific plan covering: assessment of each person's supervision need (staff and/or technology); trained substitutes; supervisor qualifications and training; and periodic review of continuing need.
The plan is a condition of the IRA operating certificate (OMR 248).
Revise the plan when residents' needs or staffing patterns change.

policies.category: IRA site-specific protective oversight plan and evacuation plan (686.16)
policies.title: Individual Protective Oversight Assessment and Annual Review
state_specifics: Each person has a plan for protective oversight based on analysis of need.
Review and revise it periodically and at least annually, and integrate it with the person's other services and ISP.
Include a current fire-evacuation evaluation in each ISP (8 or fewer beds).
Document any less intensive coverage as an individual assessment in the plan of services (686.9(a)(4)).

policies.category: IRA site-specific protective oversight plan and evacuation plan (686.16)
policies.title: Supervisor and Substitute Qualifications, Training and First Aid
state_specifics: Use appropriately trained substitute personnel when primary assigned staff are unavailable.
Set qualifications and training for those responsible for supervision. Supervisors need training suited to residents' needs, including first aid.
Parties with supervision responsibility must know each person's protective oversight plan. The plan must be implemented as written in the ISP.
Volunteers may not substitute for paid personnel (686.9(a)(3)).

policies.category: IRA site-specific protective oversight plan and evacuation plan (686.16)
policies.title: Facility Evacuation Plan, Staff and Resident Training and Evaluation
state_specifics: OPWDD verifies that the IRA has implemented a facility evacuation plan.
OPWDD verifies that staff and residents are trained and evaluated on performing the plan.
Occupants unable to evacuate in 3 minutes or less trigger 635-7.2(a)(1)(iii).
Run drills at the frequency set by ADM #2012-02. Keep drill logs.

policies.title: Supportive IRA Referral, Intake and Supervision-Need Assessment
state_specifics: Use only if the residence is certified as a supportive IRA. Staff there are typically not onsite at all times.
The intake policy must address how the agency assesses and meets the applicant's need for supervision and set the admission criteria listed in 686.8(b)(1). Pull that text.
DDRO approval and CRO admission rules (636-3) still apply.
ADM #2002-01 documentation guidance and its 11-day minimum are status-unverified. Confirm before use.

policies.title: Supportive IRA Discharge Criteria
state_specifics: Discharge criteria describe the level of independent functioning that would permit independent living and the activities that promote independence.
Criteria describe problem circumstances or declining function that might lead to a more restrictive program.
Discharge is only to a setting that can better meet the person's needs and is actually available at the projected discharge date.

policies.title: Supportive IRA Visitation, Emergency Contacts and Evacuation Training
state_specifics: A trained person must be available to visit residents in the absence of the assigned case manager.
Residents are informed whom to call in an emergency or unusual or unsettling circumstance.
All occupants are trained to evacuate in emergencies.
Add any other information specific to supportive operations.

policies.title: Individual Rights and HCBS Settings Requirements
state_specifics: Give the 633.4(a)(4) rights at or before admission and after changes, in the primary language.
Advise staff of individuals' rights (633.4(a)(6)).
Rights include visitors, communication, privacy, personal storage, own clothing, religion, voting and gender expression.
Individuals have access to food at any time.

policies.title: Rights Restrictions, Modifications and Due Process
state_specifics: Limitations must be documented, individual, time-limited and for clinical purposes only (633.4(a)(3)).
A modification of HCBS rights needs a specific assessed need and justification in the person-centered plan (636-1.4).
Rights are never limited for staff convenience, as a threat, as retribution or for discipline (633.4(a)(7)).
The person may object under 633.12.

policies.title: Nondiscrimination and Communication Access
federal: Title VI of the Civil Rights Act
state_specifics: Provide language access and interpreters at no charge (633.4(a)(15)).
Provide rights and conduct rules in the primary language.
Provide accommodations for individuals with communication or sensory needs.

policies.title: Positive Behavior Support
state_specifics: Follow 633.16 on behavior support: functional behavior assessment, a behavior support plan as part of the plan of services, and Level 1 and 2 Behavioral Intervention Specialist qualifications.
Review plans through the behavior plan/human rights committee.
Plans must not include aversive conditioning.

policies.title: Restrictive Interventions, Restraint and Seclusion
state_specifics: Restrictive/intrusive interventions under 633.16 include restrictive physical intervention, exclusionary time-out, mechanical restraining devices, and behavior medication without a co-occurring psychiatric diagnosis.
Individuals have the right to freedom from unnecessary mechanical restraint (633.4).
Deliberate inappropriate use of restraints is abuse/neglect. Inappropriate use is a significant incident. Report both to VPCR at 1-855-373-2122.
Pull the 633.16(d)-(j) operative subdivisions before finalizing.

policies.title: Missing Person and Elopement
state_specifics: Missing person is a significant incident under current 624.3 categories. Pull the text.
Report reportable incidents immediately to the CEO or designee and OPWDD (624.5).
Include each individual's elopement risk and supervision level in the protective oversight plan.

policies.title: Licensure, Certification, Provider Agreements and Temporary Use Beds
state_specifics: The IRA operating certificate (OMR 248) is triennial, with a maximum term of 3 years. Calendar renewal.
Medicaid and waiver enrollment needs an IRS SS-4 letter and a certified Provider Compliance Program. Community residence enrollment is under category of service 0269.
IRAs of 4+ beds may designate temporary use beds, which count toward certified capacity (686.15).
Notify OPWDD of changes in ownership. A criminal history check is also required (633.22).

policies.title: Quality Improvement, Data Review and Mortality Review
state_specifics: Review incidents, notable occurrences and deaths at least quarterly.
Do internal quarterly samples of claims and documentation as part of the Provider Compliance Program.
Track the deficiency dispute process from OPWDD Division of Quality Improvement (effective 4/1/2024).

policies.title: Medicaid Compliance, Billing and Service Documentation
state_specifics: Bill supervised IRA residential habilitation daily. Rate codes are service day, therapeutic/non-medical leave day and retainer/medical leave day.
A claim is disallowed if documentation does not match the code (OMIG).
Retainer days are capped at 14 per person per rate year (ADM #2014-01). Confirm it is still in effect.
The provider has one provider-wide rate (10 NYCRR 86-10.3).
EVV applicability was not confirmed. Ask OPWDD.

documents.title: 14 NYCRR § 686.6 - Administration (policy/procedure manual content required of each community residence)
documents.form_number: None. No OPWDD policy checklist form was found; 14 NYCRR 686.6 is the section that lists the required written policies.
documents.issuer: NYS Office for People With Developmental Disabilities (OPWDD), 14 NYCRR Part 686 (text via Cornell LII)
documents.version: Amended NYS Register 9/21/2016 (eff. 9/21/2016); the current LII text shows no later amendment
documents.how_used: Primary source for the policy and procedure manual. Section 686.6(a)(2) says each community residence must develop and implement policies/procedures addressing the listed topics 'at a minimum'. Section 686.6(b)(3) lists the manual contents OPWDD surveys for.

documents.title: 14 NYCRR § 686.16 - Certification of the facility class known as individualized residential alternative (site-specific protective oversight plan; evacuation plan)
documents.version: Justia text current through NYS Register 47, No. 25 (June 25, 2025)
documents.how_used: IRA-specific written plan requirements. It requires a site-specific written protective oversight plan, and OPWDD verifies a facility evacuation plan.

documents.title: 14 NYCRR § 686.8 - Program for supportive community residences (supportive CR/IRA policy additions)
documents.version: Justia text current through NYS Register 47, No. 25 (June 25, 2025)
documents.how_used: Applies only to supportive community residences. It adds referral/intake/admission and discharge-criteria policies, and extra items for the manual required by 686.6(a)(2).

required_items.text: Each community residence shall develop and implement policies/procedures which address, at a minimum:
Admission, including at least:

The process to determine an applicant's need for service, the ability of the facility to meet the ongoing needs of the individual, and consideration of the relevance of the family intactness and geographic proximity of the family.
The requirement that staff and the applicant participate in the above process, including the final determination as to the applicant's admission.
The procedures for obtaining admission.
The applicant criteria, in functional terms for admission.

The requirement that, to determine that an applicant meets the criteria prior to admission, it is necessary that the following information be reviewed: (1) the results of a medical/physical examination conducted within 90 days prior to the review; and (2) an assessment or assessments of an applicant's strengths, needs, interests and living skills completed within 90 days prior to the review.
The requirement that, no person shall be admitted over his or her objection, except by a court order.

The requirement that no person shall be excluded from a residence on the basis of race, religion, color, age, gender, national origin, or inability to pay for services. This shall not preclude a facility from establishing specific admission criteria that limit the range of the age or level of disability of the individuals, or their gender when necessitated by the overall objective of the facility.

The requirement that each applicant, or parent, guardian or correspondent as available, is informed in writing prior to admission and as changes occur of any charges (see section 686.12) and the supplies and services provided by the facility (see section 686.13), unless the applicant is a capable adult and objects to such notification to others.
Discharge, including at least:
The criteria for discharge of individuals.

The requirement that, to avoid precipitous discharge, reasonable efforts are made on the part of the community residence to meet the needs of a person before a more restrictive placement is sought and/or discharge is contemplated, taking into consideration the needs of the other individuals in the facility and the facility's available resources.
The procedures for being discharged, including the procedures governing discharge of a person against the recommendations of the program planning team.
The requirement that no overt or covert physical or psychological pressure shall be applied to prevent a person who desires to leave from doing so.
The requirement that those responsible for program planning participate in designing plans and the coordination of services for a person in the process of being discharged from the residence.

Review and appeal procedures available to individuals and their parents, guardians, or correspondents, including but not limited to appeal of the plan of services and placement decisions, which are in conformance with the regulations of the commissioner.

Community involvement, providing direction to staff and individuals as to the type of activities that will promote and nurture the involvement of the community residence with the neighborhood and community.

The means whereby individuals, in accordance with their capability, contribute to the decisionmaking process relative to the day-to-day activities at the community residence, and individual/staff involvement in neighborhood/community activities.
Requirements for the administration of the following:
plans of services;
person's financial records;
confidentiality and protection of individuals' records;
coordination, collection, release and tracking of statistical information;
incidents and allegations of abuse; and
medication administration, the current certification status of community residence staff to administer medications, and the self-administration of medication training program for individuals.

Medical emergencies, other potential emergencies, evacuation procedures to meet the special needs of persons with developmental disabilities, and disasters; the necessary staff actions associated with these situations; and the means to familiarize staff with these policies and procedures.
Health and safety issues.
Personnel policies/procedures addressing at least:
the recruitment and hiring process; qualifications, education and skills required; job descriptions; description of duties and responsibilities; and job performance evaluations;

staff training programs which include at a minimum: (1) coordination of staff development and training that is consistent with individuals' and staff needs and agency/facility policies; (2) orientation procedures; (3) in-service training; and (4) the use of community training resources;
the means whereby matters of concern to staff can be made known without threat of job loss; and
the prohibition of discrimination in hiring and promotion based on race, religion, color, gender, national origin, age or disability.
The approval process for policies/procedures, which includes a description of the role of the governing body in this process.
The agency/facility policy/procedure manual is a public document and, as such, shall be available to individuals, parents, guardians, correspondents, staff and others.

A written policy/procedure manual(s) exists with contents addressing the following areas: (i) admission and discharge of individuals; (ii) administration of records; (iii) emergencies and disasters; (iv) health and safety issues; (v) personnel; (vi) review and appeal procedures for concerns of individuals and their correspondents; (vii) community involvement of staff and individuals; and (viii) individuals' involvement in community residence activities.

The agency/facility has written criteria for a residence manager which mandate that the person in the position has, at a minimum, been awarded a high school diploma or its equivalent and has at least one year of experience working with persons with developmental disabilities.

A facility receiving an operating certificate as an individualized residential alternative, shall develop a site specific written plan for protective oversight. The plan shall include provisions for ensuring:
The assessment of each person's need for the amount and type of supervision necessary including both staff and/or technology as appropriate to the person and circumstance.
The use of appropriately trained substitute personnel when the primary assigned personnel are unavailable.
The establishment of qualifications and training requirements of those responsible for supervision.
The establishment of a process whereby the person's continuing need for the originally recommended amount and type of protective oversight can be periodically reviewed, and modified as necessary.
Each facility in this class shall ensure the provision of, or provide as its minimum responsibility, protective oversight (see glossary) appropriate to the person's needs.

OPWDD shall verify that each individualized residential alternative has implemented a facility evacuation plan. OPWDD shall verify that staff and persons residing in the facility are trained and evaluated regarding their performance of said plan.

OPWDD shall verify that each person has a plan for protective oversight, based on an analysis of the person's need for same, and that such need has periodically, but at least annually, been reviewed, revised as appropriate, and integrated, as appropriate, with other services received.

OPWDD shall verify that persons living in the facility are receiving appropriate protective oversight in accordance with the following: (i) any parties with supervision responsibilities have received training appropriate to the protective oversight needs of the persons in the facility including, but not limited to, first aid; (ii) any parties with supervision responsibilities are aware of the specifics of each person's plan for protective oversight; and (iii) each person's plan for protective oversight is being implemented as specified in the person's individualized service plan.
The agency/facility shall develop policies/procedures governing referral, intake and admission. (Supportive community residences)

These policies and procedures shall specifically address how the agency/facility will assess and meet the applicant's need for supervision in the supportive community residence, and shall include criteria justifying admission as listed in paragraph (b)(1) of this section.

There shall be discharge criteria which: (i) describe the level of independent functioning that would appropriately permit a person to live independently; and identify those activities and experiences which would promote such increased independence; (ii) describe potential problem circumstances or degenerating person functioning level which might result in discharge to a more restrictive program; and (iii) preclude discharge except to a setting which can more appropriately meet the person's needs and such a setting is actually available at the time of projected discharge.

The policy and procedure manual, as required in section 686.6(a)(2) of this Part shall also incorporate: (i) the requirement that a trained person shall be available to make visitations to a person in a supportive community residence in the absence of the assigned case manager; (ii) the requirement that a person shall be informed of the persons to call in the event of an emergency or other unusual or unsettling circumstances; (iii) the requirement that all occupants of a supportive community residence shall be trained to evacuate the facility in emergency situations; and (iv) any other necessary information specific to the operation of a supportive community residence.

official.notes: No single OPWDD policy checklist or form was found, so the required items come from regulation sections that list required written policies. The IRA Operating Certificate Application (OMR 248, cited in your source list) could not be retrieved: the businessexpress.ny.gov page returned a permission error, and searches did not surface the form. If you can get OMR 248 from OPWDD, check it against this list. (1) The manual is the agency's policy/procedure manual under 686.6(a)(2). OPWDD's stated intent in 686.2(b) is that the policies reflect compliance with Part 686 and become part of the agency's/facility's manual(s).
